text:
Sam W: FYI - getting a fresh escalation. Multiple Dedicated customers (acme & stayfit) seeing huge cold-starts this morning, 429s on initial bursts. First report at 07:02PT.
Maya P: Ack. Any repro steps or logs from the customer?
Sam W: Customer sent timeline + a quick repro curl hitting their dedicated endpoint. They see requests queueing ~20-35s before model pod becomes Ready. When Ready they get 200 but latency spikes. They also saw 401s just before the 429s for a short window.
Nate C: Customer message: "Our checkout timed out during morning ramp, we saw 429s and timeouts. Billing token rotation happened ~07:00."
Jordan L: Noted. Possible two things: (1) auth token rotation causing attach retries, (2) image pull/backoff or probe failures causing pods to be unready and autoscaler not counting them. Any kube events?
Priya K: Pulled their support bundle. Quick grep shows repeated kubelet imagepull backoff for model-serve-init container around 07:01–07:04, mixed with attach auth errors to registry for a short window.
Sam W: Here's the customer's simplified repro they ran:

```bash
for i in {1..50}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://dedicated.redwood.io/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"x","max_tokens":16}' &
done
wait
```

They get a stream of 429s for the first 30s, then responses arrive in bursts.
Maya P: Can you paste the relevant logs? Even a few lines helps.
Priya K: From the bundle (anonymized):

```
Jul 07 07:01:12 kubelet[...]: ImagePullBackOff: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to pull image: unauthorized
Jul 07 07:01:15 attach-controller[...]: auth: token exchange failed for tenant=acme, err=invalid_grant
Jul 07 07:01:20 autoscaler[...]: probe failure count=6 target=dedicated-pool-42
Jul 07 07:01:40 scheduler[...]: pod will remain Pending: init container restartLoopBackOff
```

Priya K: Looks like registry auth rotation coincided with probe flapping. When registry pulls fail, pods never reach Ready -> warm pool remains depleted -> autoscaler sees no healthy pods to route and scales slowly because each new pod does init (large model), causing a cascade.
Jordan L: Also see our autoscaler uses conservative backoff to avoid thrash. If probes fail repeatedly, autoscaler may respect minReplicas and wait for successful readiness before adding more replicas. Combined with imagepull backoff and auth rotation, we get a stall.
Maya P: Could be noisy tenant too. If other tenants consumed pull bandwidth or hit registry rate limits, backoffs amplify.
Sam W: Customer noted a spike from another tenant earlier that morning. They suspected noisy neighbor. They tagged it as "highly coincident" with their issue.
Nate C: Customer asked for immediate mitigations they'd accept.
Priya K: Short-term mitigations:
- Increase min_replicas for their Dedicated pool to keep warm pods.
- Add a short pre-pull step or warm-pool reserve (we can schedule a rollout to set min_replicas=3 during peak hours).
- Advise customer to delay heavy workloads during auth rotations until rotation completes (not ideal).
Jordan L: Platform-side mitigations:
- Fix registry auth rotation to use rolling credentials so imagepulls are uninterrupted.
- Add fallback to use cached local images for 5m after rotation.
- Reduce autoscaler add-rate backoff for known warmup-critical tiers (allow emergency burst spinup).
Maya P: Any quick workaround we can apply now for acme? They want a stopgap.
Sam W: I proposed temporary min_replicas bump to 3 and increasing attach retry timeout to avoid marking pods as failing during transient auth errors. Customer approved.
Priya K: Applying min_replicas bump now. Running hg:

```
kubectl -n dedicated set resources deployment/dedicated-pool-42 --replicas=3
```

deploy-bot: Deploy queued by Priya K for dedicated-pool-42: scale to 3 replicas. ETA ~2m :rocket:
Jordan L: I'll open a follow-up ticket with infra to audit registry rotation logs and tenant rate-limits. Also want to add telemetry: correlate imagepull backoffs with autoscaler stalls.
Nate C: Customer confirmed partial relief after ~4m; error rate dropped and latency returned near normal. They're still nervous, asked for postmortem and permanent fix.
Maya P: Great. We'll draft an incident summary and recommended remediation. Priya, Jordan — please add repro steps and timeline to the ticket.
Sam W: Putting someone on postmortem: Maya leading, Jordan+Priya supporting. I'll include the customer's bundle and our actions. Closing thread here and moving to incident matrix.
Maya P: Thanks all. :thumbsup!
